Map new samples to a self-organising map

Source: R/cluster_functions.R
eemsom_predict.Rd

New EEMs are assigned to their best matching unit. For maps of EEMs (eemsom), they are normalised like the training data. For maps of PARAFAC loadings (eempf_som), their loadings are calculated first with the fixed emission and excitation loadings of the PARAFAC model (A_missing).

Usage

eemsom_predict(som, eem_list, cores = 1, ...)

Arguments

som

object of class eemsom, see eemsom or eempf_som

eem_list

object of class eemlist with the same excitation and emission wavelengths as the training data or the PARAFAC model

cores

number of cores used by A_missing (maps of PARAFAC loadings only)

...

additional arguments passed on to A_missing and eem_parafac (maps of PARAFAC loadings only), e.g. maxit. By default, nstart = 1 is used because the loadings with fixed B and C modes do not depend on the start.

Value

data frame with columns sample, unit, x, y, distance, hits, umatrix and cluster like eemsom_samples. hits is the number of training samples mapped to the unit. A distance much higher than the distances of the training samples indicates a sample that is not represented by the map.

Details

Maps of EEMs: only the wavelength pairs used in the map are considered. Missing values in the new samples are ignored when calculating the distances, which are scaled up to the number of all wavelength pairs as in kohonen (see eemsom_samples).

Maps of PARAFAC loadings: the new EEMs need the same preparation as the EEMs of the PARAFAC model (e.g. scatter removal). Their Fmax loadings are scaled like in eempf_som (relative or absolute) and the distances refer to these loadings.

See also

Other map results: eemsom_codes(), eemsom_quality(), eemsom_samples(), eemsom_split()

Examples

data(eem_list)

som <- eemsom(eem_list, rlen = 100, seed = 42)
som <- eemsom_cluster(som, k = 3)
# usually, new samples are mapped. Here, the training samples are used.
eemsom_predict(som, eem_list)

# map of PARAFAC loadings: the loadings of the new samples are calculated first
data(pf_models)
data(eem_list_outliers)
pfsom <- eempf_som(pf4[[1]], rlen = 100, seed = 42)
new_samples <- eem_list_outliers |>
  eem_rem_scat(remove_scatter = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE),
               remove_scatter_width = c(15, 15, 18, 19)) |>
  eem_interp(type = 1, extend = FALSE, cores = 1)
eemsom_predict(pfsom, new_samples)
#>       sample unit   x        y   distance hits    umatrix cluster
#> 1 dsfb676psp   46 1.0 8.660254 0.06066783    7 0.02492000      NA
#> 2  dsgb447wt   25 5.5 4.330127 0.05285394    6 0.01610523      NA
